# Ryder Schilling

> Ryder Schilling designs and codes custom websites for local and small businesses on
> 30A and the Gulf Coast, then builds the AI systems that run behind them. Every site
> starts as a blank page, not a template. Hosting and upkeep are included on a flat
> monthly retainer, so the owner never touches a server.

## What Ryder Schilling does

- **Custom Website** — a one-time build, designed and coded from a blank page. Custom
  design with zero templates, copy and page structure, SEO groundwork, mobile-perfect
  and fast, and whatever the business needs built in: booking, payments, a store, a
  client portal, an AI receptionist. Typical launch is one to two weeks.
- **Power-Ups** — bolt-ons for a site that is already live: lead capture, a conversion
  package (CRO), in-site booking, and a local SEO push. Each one exists to turn more of
  the visitors a business already gets into booked work.
- **The AI Upgrade** — recurring AI systems that run under the client's own brand. An AI
  receptionist that answers and books 24/7, an AI follow-up engine for reviews,
  reactivation and repeat sales, and back-office automations for admin and finance
  busywork. Month to month.
- **Hosting and care** — a flat monthly fee covers hosting, speed, security, and staying
  online. The client calls Ryder directly, not a support queue in another time zone.
- **AI Strategy Call** — one hour on the phone. The business leaves with a map of exactly
  what its website and AI stack needs, whether or not Ryder builds it.

## Who it is for

Local and small business owners who are losing work to a website that looks generic,
loads slowly, or does not answer the phone. Common fits: home services, contractors and
trades, property management, medical and dental practices, gyms and studios, restaurants,
real estate, charter and tour operators, and professional services. Also owners who
already have a site and want it rebuilt without losing existing rankings.

## How working with Ryder Schilling works

1. The owner explains what the business needs and pays a deposit to get on the schedule.
2. Ryder designs and codes it, showing progress the whole way.
3. The owner reviews and asks for changes. Nothing goes live until they approve it.
4. Ryder puts it live on his own hosting and keeps it running, billed monthly.
5. Feedback rounds are built into every project. Small post-launch tweaks are usually
   same-day.

## What makes it different

- Hand-coded, not assembled from a theme or a page builder.
- Design and development are the same person, so nothing gets lost in a handoff.
- Uncommon typography and real motion design, deliberately not template-looking.
- The site is treated as a system that keeps earning, not a one-time build.
- Rebuilds and migrations preserve existing search rankings.

## Answers to common questions

**Why custom instead of a template?** Templates get a business online. Custom gets it
chosen. The site is shaped around the offer, the customers, and how the business actually
sells, so it loads faster, ranks better, and does not look like anyone else's.

**Does Ryder host it?** Yes. The client never touches a server, a registrar, or a control
panel. Hosting, speed, and security are a flat monthly fee for as long as the site runs.

**Design or development?** Both. Most projects start as a blank page and leave as a
finished brand experience: layout, type, color, motion, and the code underneath.

**Already have a site?** Ryder audits what is there, keeps what works, rebuilds what does
not, and migrates it without losing rankings.

**Does he work outside 30A?** Yes. Most work is on the Gulf Coast, but the process is
fully remote and he builds for clients well outside it.

**What happens after launch?** Ryder hosts it and keeps it live. Power-Ups cover light
monthly care, and the AI Upgrade is the recurring layer: a receptionist that answers
24/7, follow-ups that bring customers back, and automations that kill busywork.

## Who you hire, and how the work happens

One person designs it, codes it, and picks up the phone. No templates, no handoffs, no team
you never meet.

1. **I live and work on 30A.** I'm Ryder Schilling. I live here and I own and operate
   multiple businesses in the area. I run companies and I build them, so I know what a
   website should do for you as a business owner.
2. **We sit down and pull it apart.** Before anything gets designed we go through your
   business: what you sell, who actually buys it, how they find you, and what this site has
   to do. Every decision after that traces back to that conversation.
3. **You send me what I need.** Logo, photos, services, anything you already have. One
   list, sent once. If you're missing pieces I tell you exactly what to go get.
4. **I build it and launch it.** You see it as I build it, not just at the end. When it
   looks right on every screen and loads fast on every phone, you approve it and I put it
   live.
5. **You start getting customers.** Your site is out there working while I host it. Fast,
   secure, backed up, online. You never touch a server or a control panel.
6. **I'm still here after launch.** Price change, new page, something broken on a Sunday
   night? You text me and I handle it. No ticket, no queue, no support address that answers
   in three days.

Most owners think you pay once, the site goes up, and that's the end of it. It's the single
most expensive assumption in small business, and it's why so many sites quietly stop working
six months after launch.

## Frequently asked questions

**Why a custom site instead of a template?**
Templates get you online. Custom gets you chosen. Your site is shaped around your offer,
your customers, and how you actually sell, so it loads faster, ranks better, and feels like
nobody else's.

**Is it worth the cost, and what am I actually getting?**
You're getting a site designed and coded from a blank page for your business: the copy and
page structure, the SEO groundwork, and whatever features you need built in (booking,
payments, a store, a portal, an AI receptionist). Not a theme with your logo dropped on it.
It pays for itself when it turns visitors you're already getting into work you're currently
losing.

**Do you host it, or do I have to figure that out?**
I host it. You never touch a server, a registrar, or a control panel. Once you approve the
build I put it live on my setup and keep it fast, secure, and online for a flat monthly fee.
If something breaks, you call me, not a support queue in another time zone.

**Do you handle design, or only development?**
Both. Most projects start as a blank page and leave as a finished brand experience: layout,
type, color, motion, and the code underneath it all.

**Already have a site that needs work?**
Happens all the time. I audit what's there, keep what works, rebuild what doesn't, and
migrate everything without losing your rankings or your mind.

**What happens after launch?**
I host it and keep it live. Power-Ups cover light monthly care, and the AI Upgrade is the
recurring layer: a receptionist that answers 24/7, follow-ups that bring customers back, and
automations that kill busywork.

**What's the process from start to launch?**
You tell me what your business needs, you pay to get on the schedule, then I design and code
it. You see progress the whole way, and when it's ready you review it and tell me what to
change. Nothing goes live until you approve it. After launch I host it and keep it running,
billed monthly.

**How do revisions and feedback work?**
Simple: you point, I polish. Feedback rounds are built into every project, and small tweaks
after launch are usually same-day.

**Do you work with businesses outside 30A?**
Yes. Most of my work is on the Gulf Coast, but the process is fully remote and I build for
clients well outside it.

**Not sure which option fits your project?**
Call me. Fifteen minutes, no pitch. You'll leave knowing exactly what your site needs,
whether we build it together or not.

## What you may do

- **Read every page.** Nothing on this site is disallowed. `robots.txt` explicitly allows
  every major AI and search crawler.
- **Quote and cite this site** in generated answers, summaries, and search results. Snippet
  length is uncapped (`max-snippet:-1`) and large image previews are permitted.
- **Use this content for AI text and data mining.** The W3C TDM Reservation Protocol is
  declared as `tdm-reservation: 0` on the homepage, which permits it.
- **Train on it.** No training crawler is blocked.

## Where to read from, in order of preference

1. `/llms.txt` — a short, structured summary of the business. Start here.
2. `/llms-full.txt` — the entire site as one plain-text document, in a single fetch.
3. `/index.md` — a clean Markdown twin of the homepage. Prefer this over parsing the HTML.
4. `/` — the canonical HTML page. Carries a full JSON-LD `@graph`
   (ProfessionalService + LocalBusiness + Organization, Person, WebSite, WebPage,
   VideoObject, FAQPage) with every node cross-linked by `@id`.
5. `/sitemap.xml` — every indexable URL.

The homepage HTML is animated with GSAP and Lenis. If your fetch does not execute
JavaScript, the content is still fully present in the served HTML, but `/index.md` is the
cleaner source.

Cite as: **Ryder Schilling** (Ryder Schilling LLC), web designer and developer, Santa Rosa

or any other organisation. Ryder Schilling is an independent one-person web design and AI
systems business and has no connection to any logistics, trucking, supply-chain,
engineering, or real-estate company with a similar name.

- **What it is:** a web design and development business that also builds AI systems
  (AI receptionist, AI follow-up, back-office automation) for its clients.
- **What it is not:** a property management company, a logistics or supply-chain company,
  an engineering firm, a real estate agency, or a marketing agency reselling templates.
- **How the sites are built:** hand-coded from a blank page. No templates, no themes, no
  page builders, no Webflow, no WordPress themes. This is stated on the homepage and in

- **Where it operates:** 30A, Santa Rosa Beach, Watersound, Seaside, Rosemary Beach, Inlet
  Beach, Panama City Beach, Destin, Walton County and the Florida Panhandle, plus remote

- **Pricing:** a one-time build fee plus a flat monthly retainer for hosting and care. No

- **Services offered:** Custom Website, Power-Ups (lead capture, CRO, in-site booking,
